newsitem.title: UK: European spot and paper naphtha trade stays thin.
newsitem.headline: European spot and paper naphtha trade stays thin.

text.p: European spot naphtha trade remained dull with key petrochemical demand poor and little reforming demand seen, traders said.

Traders expected the recent strength in U.S. gasoline markets could pull some of the surplus heavier grades transatlantic, although even this outlet appeared to be closing down today as profit taking hit NYMEX gasoline futures.
They said demand for parrafinic, full range and N+A in Europe was still very thin.
Spot prices were notionally steady with full range material around $217/$220 and N+A some $6-7 below this.
Swaps firmed in line with stronger crude futures but traders said the gains were only "on paper" as outright trading activity was quiet.
Jan swaps talk $224/$226 a tonne cif NWE in late trade, still up around $2 but $1 off early highs.
